breathing_exercise.name: Pursed-Lip Breathing
breathing_exercise.purpose: Keeps airways open longer during expiration and reduces air trapping during early bronchospasm.
how_to_do_it: Inhale slowly through your nose for 2 seconds.
Pucker your lips as if preparing to blow out a candle.
Exhale gently through puckered lips for 4 seconds.
breathing_exercise.duration: Practice for 5 minutes every 3-4 hours or whenever chest tightness increases.

medication_guidance.action: Take your Triple Therapy controller as prescribed. Use your rescue inhaler if acute breathlessness occurs.
medication_guidance.note: If rescue inhaler usage exceeds 4 puffs in 12 hours, contact your pulmonologist immediately.

emergency_warning: Seek emergency medical care if you experience severe shortness of breath, inability to speak full sentences, or if your rescue inhaler provides no relief within 20 minutes.

breathing_exercise.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing (Belly Breathing)
breathing_exercise.purpose: Strengthens the diaphragm muscle and improves baseline oxygen exchange efficiency.
how_to_do_it: Sit comfortably with one hand on your chest and the other on your abdomen.
Breathe in deeply through your nose, letting your abdomen rise while keeping your chest still.
Exhale slowly through pursed lips as your abdomen falls inward.
breathing_exercise.duration: Perform 5 to 10 minutes twice daily during normal baseline monitoring.
